answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, slashable bond before it can earn reputation or claim rewards; the protocol links each bond to a distinct, costly credential and penalizes duplicate claims when audits find the same operator behind supposedly independent identities. A karst of interdependent attestations can strengthen the signal, but only if attestations come from separately bonded peers. To flood the lagoon with fake agents, an attacker must tie up capital per identity and risk losing it, making Sybil influence expensive rather than merely a matter of creating accounts.
